Revenue / Campaign contribution

Return on ad spend (ROAS)

Attributed net sales revenue per unit of media spend for a defined attribution model and window. This revenue-based version uses sales after the agreed refund and discount treatment, rather than assigning arbitrary revenue to a form submission.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Attributed net sales revenue per unit of media spend for a defined attribution model and window. This revenue-based version uses sales after the agreed refund and discount treatment, rather than assigning arbitrary revenue to a form submission.

×

How we use it

We connect ad data to actual sales records and show contribution alongside ROAS. A higher multiple provides more revenue for each unit of media cost under the chosen attribution rules.

Transparent calculationAttributed net sales revenue ÷ attributed media spend
attributed net sales30,000
media spend6,000

30,000 ÷ 6,000 = 5× ROAS, equivalent to 500% when a platform displays ROAS as a percentage.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Campaign and attribution model
  • Product and market
  • Customer cohort and return window

Questions we investigate

  • Are returns and discounts reflected in net sales?
  • Does attribution assign the same sales repeatedly?
  • Does high ROAS still leave positive contribution?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Reconcile attributed net sales to commerce records.
  • Review margin and contribution alongside ROAS.
  • Compare campaigns within consistent attribution windows.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Paid media and finance leads
Weekly provisionally; monthly after returns reconcile.

Required data

  • Attributed net sales and matching media spend
  • Refund, discount, and order identifiers
  • Attribution model, currency, and reporting window

Read the measure with context

Zero media spend makes ROAS undefined. ROAS is not profit or causal lift. Platforms can claim overlapping sales, and modeled conversion values may differ from collected sales. Match currencies, revenue adjustments, and conversion delays before comparison.
